result.document_summary: Part 3 of 4 of the New Jersey DCA landlord-tenant information publication, covering habitability remedies and the Anti-Eviction Act's good-cause eviction requirements, causes, notices and relocation assistance.
result.notes: Only one in-scope rule extracted: the NJ Anti-Eviction Act (just cause eviction). The rest of this part (utilities, receivership, lead paint, drinking water, habitability remedies, flood notices, crime insurance, self-help eviction procedure) is outside the six categories. The text of this part cuts off mid-cause N; coverage and effective date are not stated in this part. Rent-increase, deposit and screening content, if any, would be in other parts.

rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act (good cause required to evict)
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may remove a tenant or refuse to renew a lease only for a statutory good cause and through a court judgment for possession. Each cause except nonpayment requires a written Notice to Quit with a cause-specific period (3 days to 3 years), some causes need a prior Notice to Cease, and removal for substantial health and safety violations requires relocation assistance first.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; Notice to Quit periods from 3 days up to 3 years depending on cause; relocation assistance of 6 times monthly rent for illegal occupancy evictions
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and mobile home park land, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding houses.

exemptions.label: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units

all_of.text: two- or three-unit premises with two or fewer rental units

exemptions.label: Hotel, motel or guest house rented to transient or seasonal guest

all_of.text: hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant

exemptions.label: Unit held in trust for developmentally disabled family member who permanently occupies it

all_of.value: unit held in trust for immediate family member who is developmentally disabled and permanently occupies it
all_of.text: a unit held in trust on behalf of a member of the immediate family, if that family member is developmentally disabled, and permanently occupies the dwelling unit

rules.exemptions_text: Not applicable to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units, hotel/motel/guest-house transient or seasonal guests (unless the occupant has no alternate residence and resides there continually), or a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it.
rules.interaction: Rent increases underlying a nonpayment-of-increase eviction must comply with other laws and municipal ordinances, including rent control. Condominium/cooperative conversion evictions must also comply with the conversion regulations and the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act.
